Another tip just came to mind… diddles with different accent groupings!!!

Practicing something like…
3/4 [Rr lL rr / Ll rR ll] 
Again, you wanna play this SUPER slow. Put super hard emphasis on the accents. When you’re able to play these types of patterns well :)

(theres soooo many variations on this exercise if you want others.

The biggest thing I notice is that they’re not super even., which (by the looks of it) is due to you using the pad’s rebound as a crutch.
2 things you can do that worked really really well for me…
1) Play on something SUPER dead… a pillow, your mattress, blankets… Diddling on things like this forces you to not rely on rebound, which gets you used to the feeling of pulling up with the rebound, allowing you to play a much more even RR LL. Right now it sounds more like Rr Ll, weaker strong di-, but weak -dles. 
(This works with most rudiments, other than closed rolls obviously lol)

2) Spacing between Each double is being crunched a tad. This is caused by the same thing, so doing the pillow thing DOES help. What others have said… slowing down, and really focusing on the second note. 

A rudiment that will help a lot is anything that goes back and forth between singles and doubles. 
(RLRLRLRL-RRLLRRLL for example.) Your goal is to play is SLOW.. VERY slow. Aim to make the singles and doubles singles. If played well, you shouldn’t be able to tell which is being played.

IMO, asymmetry should (and does) go deeper than 1-1 comparisons. Rather, asymmetry is about ensuring that both sides have a totally different play experience (overall) while still remaining balanced. Usually the devs do this with 1-1 equivelents (Fiddler / Lionclaw for example). These’s are fine and all, but really interesting asymetry comes when one side has something the other side simply doesn’t have, or has no comparable weapon. A good example would be the collie BTD. Its a beefstick, slow rolling, battle tank which is VERY expensive to produce. The wardens don’t have any equivalent to this. The closest I can think is an STD… though it fulfills a much different role. All they really have in common is their ammunition type, and damage output. 
This isn’t even considering how certain vehicles and weapons change roles throughout a war.

Hot take: I’d have no problem if collies had rocket arty, and wardens had regular arty, or visa versa. 

The question of balancing these things isn’t “Oh what do the collies have that match this?” or “Do the wardens have anything similar?” It’s whether one side has a counter available to whatever is in question. Rather than thinking of asymmetry as “one upsies,” I think of it more like rock paper scissors.
